rows.selection_reason: With no prior evidence, the goal is to establish a strong baseline while gaining information about multiple key design dimensions simultaneously. config_048 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) combines the strongest available components: a purpose-built single-cell foundation model (scgpt) for RNA, a large pretrained ViT-L for images, transformer-based aggregation for expressive multi-profile integration, and weighted fusion to let the model learn modality importance. If this performs well, it confirms the multimodal + strong-encoder direction and I can ablate individual components in later experiments. If it underperforms, it signals that complexity (transformer aggregation, ViT-L, or weighted fusion) may be harmful, directing exploration toward simpler alternatives. This single experiment reduces uncertainty across four major design axes (model type, encoder quality, aggregation, fusion) and sets a high bar for the remaining 9 experiments.

With only one completed experiment (config_048: multimodal, scgpt+imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted → acc 0.520), the largest remaining uncertainty is whether the multimodal fusion actually adds value over a strong unimodal baseline. Config_022 (image_only, multiprofile, imagenet_vit_l, transformer) is a clean ablation: it keeps the same image encoder and aggregation strategy as config_048, removing only the RNA modality and fusion step. If image-only performs comparably (~0.52), the RNA contribution is marginal and I should redirect remaining budget toward unimodal optimization or simpler multimodal variants. If image-only is substantially worse, it confirms that multimodal fusion is worth pursuing and justifies investing the remaining 7 experiments in refining the multimodal configuration (encoder choices, aggregation, fusion). This single experiment resolves the highest-impact design question before committing further budget.

Evidence: config_048 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) achieved the best accuracy (0.520), while image-only (config_022) was weak (0.260), confirming that the multimodal scgpt+ViT-L backbone with transformer aggregation is the strongest direction. Uncertainty: we have not tested whether the weighted fusion is optimal or whether simple concatenation (concat) of the two modal embeddings could yield a stronger signal. This experiment (config_015) isolates exactly one variable—fusion strategy (weighted → concat)—while holding all other components at their known-best settings. It is the best next experiment because it is a clean, minimal ablation of the highest-leverage architectural choice in the current best config, and the result will directly inform whether to exploit the weighted-fusion path or pivot to concat-fusion for the remaining 7 experiments.

The current best (config_048, acc=0.520) uses scgpt as the RNA encoder with imagenet_vit_l, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion. The image-only baseline (0.260) confirms multimodal fusion is critical, and weighted fusion slightly edges out concat (0.520 vs 0.507). However, we have no evidence on whether scgpt is the optimal RNA encoder. config_003 is a clean single-variable swap: it replaces scgpt with scvi_n200 while keeping all other settings identical to the current best (imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted, multiprofile, multimodal). This directly tests whether the learned generative RNA representation (scgpt) is meaningfully superior to the variational autoencoder (scvi_n200), reducing uncertainty on a fundamental architectural choice before committing remaining budget to fine-tuning aggregation or image encoder variants.

Evidence: config_003 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) achieved 0.725 acc, far outperforming scgpt-based configs (~0.52). The only other tested fusion variant (config_015, scgpt+concat) was ~1.3 pts below its weighted counterpart (config_048), suggesting weighted fusion may be important but the gap was small. Question: Does the fusion method (weighted vs concat) matter when paired with the superior scvi_n200 encoder? config_046 changes only fusion from weighted to concat while keeping all other settings identical to the current best (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, multiprofile). This is the cleanest single-variable ablation against the best config, giving unambiguous evidence about whether weighted fusion is a meaningful lever or whether concat is equally effective. With 5 experiments remaining, resolving this design choice early informs whether to focus subsequent budget on image encoder or aggregation variations.

Evidence: config_003 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) achieved the best accuracy (0.7250), and the RNA encoder (scvi_n200 vs scgpt) is clearly the dominant factor (~0.21 gap). Fusion method (weighted vs concat) shows only a marginal difference (0.7250 vs 0.7207). The image encoder dimension remains unexplored for the top-performing RNA encoder. Question: Does resnet50 match or exceed imagenet_vit_l when paired with scvi_n200, transformer, and weighted fusion? This is a clean single-variable change from the best config. Why this is the best use of experiment 6: It reduces uncertainty on the second-most-important design axis (image encoder) while keeping all proven settings fixed. If resnet50 performs comparably, it confirms the current config is near-optimal and we can focus remaining budget on fine-tuning; if it underperforms significantly, it validates imagenet_vit_l and narrows the search space for experiments 7-10.

The evidence strongly establishes scvi_n200 as the dominant RNA encoder (0.71–0.73 vs 0.51–0.52 for scgpt), and the current best (config_003, acc=0.725) uses scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted. However, all scvi_n200 experiments to date have used transformer aggregation; no avgpool variant has been tested with this encoder. Config_007 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) is a clean, single-variable change from the current best, directly testing whether the transformer aggregation is truly necessary or whether a simpler pooling strategy matches or exceeds it. If avgpool performs comparably, it confirms robustness and frees a later experiment for finer-tuning; if it underperforms, it confirms transformer is critical and narrows the search. With 3 experiments remaining after this one, reducing uncertainty on the aggregation dimension—while holding the other three parameters at their best-known values—is the highest-information use of this slot.

Evidence: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted (config_003) is the current best at 0.725 acc, and all tested multiprofile scvi_n200 variants cluster around 0.71–0.725, suggesting we are near the ceiling of the multiprofile architecture. The singleprofile setting (aggregation=None) has never been tested with the top-performing encoders (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l). This experiment tests whether the singleprofile architecture, which bypasses the transformer/avgpool aggregation step, can either match or exceed the multiprofile best by handling the two modalities differently. Choosing weighted fusion (config_051) over concat is supported by the consistent (if small) edge of weighted over concat in multiprofile (0.725 vs 0.721). With only 2 experiments remaining, this is the highest-information test: if singleprofile beats 0.725, we find a new best; if it doesn't, we confirm multiprofile is optimal and can spend the final experiment on a minor multiprofile refinement rather than chasing a dead end.

The best result so far is config_003 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.725 accuracy. All tested scvi_n200 variants confirm this architecture is near-optimal, but pca_n2000 has never been tested in the multimodal setting with the best image encoder, aggregation, and fusion. Config_043 isolates the RNA encoder variable (pca_n2000 vs scvi_n200) while holding all other hyperparameters at their best-known values, directly testing whether a simpler linear projection could match or exceed the learned scvi representation. With only 1 experiment remaining after this, this is the highest-information experiment: if pca_n2000 performs comparably, the last experiment can explore a further refinement; if it underperforms significantly, it confirms config_003 as the optimal configuration and the final experiment can be used for a minor perturbation around it.

Evidence: The top-4 experiments all use scvi_n200 + multiprofile + transformer, with config_003 (scvi_n200, ViT-L, transformer, weighted) at 0.725 being the best. The consistent pattern shows scvi_n200 >> scgpt/pca, transformer > avgpool, and ViT-L ≥ resnet50. Uncertainty: We have not tested the scvi_n200 + resnet50 + transformer + concat combination, which is the closest untested variant in the best-performing family. This experiment tests whether the concat fusion with resnet50 under transformer aggregation can approach the 0.71–0.72 range established by config_012 (weighted, 0.713). As the final experiment, config_025 has the highest expected accuracy among all remaining untested configurations (~0.70–0.71), making it the best use of the last budget slot to either confirm the ceiling or provide a small improvement over the current best.
